incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - KV-cache OOM surge detected on hosted-runtime (us-west-2). Alerting oncall (Mike K.). Error spike started ~20:42 UTC. Affected service: kvcache-prefetch + continuous-batcher. See /incidents/1890004321 for context.

Mike K.: I'm oncall, ack. grabbing logs now. any immediate customer impact? :eyes:

Sara L.: yes -- we've got elevated 502/504s for generation routes that request long contexts. correlation: large single-tenant sessions with repeated prefetch growth. sample metrics: kvcache.keys ~ +640k in 3m, mem.rss climbed to node OOM. tenant id: t-4891 shows sustained 900k token window.

Jordan P.: can we confirm whether prefetcher is allowed to grow unbounded for hosted tenants? I thought we had a soft cap.

Sara L.: looks like prefetcher backpressure didn't kick because continuous-batcher kept issuing speculative fetches for predicted seq lengths. There's a regression in the predictor logic from last week's rollout (commit sha: 0f4b3d7). gist of logs:

```
2026-03-15T20:42:11Z kvcache[hosted-0] ERROR OOM: alloc failed 52GB requested
2026-03-15T20:42:11Z kvcache[hosted-0] INFO tenant=t-4891 seq_len=1_200_143 prefetch_window=65536
2026-03-15T20:42:12Z batcher[hosted] WARN backlog=128 inflight=24
```

Mike K.: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle/disable prefetch for hosted tier, 2) enable aggressive eviction on kvcache nodes, 3) reduce continuous-batcher max_batch_tokens and inflight, 4) apply a per-tenant hard context cap (65k) as an emergency limit. doing steps 1+2 now.

Xavier R.: I can roll the batcher config hotfix. patch to apply:

```
kubectl -n hosted-runtime patch cm continuous-batcher --type merge -p '{"data": {"max_batch_tokens": "4096", "max_inflight": "12", "prefetch_enabled": "false"}}'
```

Jordan P.: I'll patch runtime env to enforce per-tenant cap and restart affected kvcache pods:

```
kubectl -n hosted-runtime set env deployment/kvcache KVCACHE_PER_TENANT_MAX_CONTEXT=65536
kubectl -n hosted-runtime rollout restart deployment/kvcache
```

Mike K.: doing eviction toggle via admin API now:

```
curl -X POST "https://internal-admin.redwood/api/kvcache/eviction" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"mode":"aggressive","target_free_mb": 8000}'
```

ops-bot: autoscaling triggered: +3 kvcache nodes requested (reason: high rss). New nodes provisioning.

(5m later)

Sara L.: update: after disabling prefetch + eviction toggle, OOMs stopped on the first node. error rate dropped from ~8.2% to 1.1% for generation endpoints. still seeing a few large backlog spikes while batcher restarts.

Xavier R.: rolling hotfix now. patch applied to continuous-batcher config across hosted cluster, will rollout in canary then prod. verifying canary traffic.

Jordan P.: added a temporary rate limit on long-context routes to prevent single-tenant abuse: gateway rule applied -> max_context_tokens_per_request=100000 for hosted (was unlimited). rule id: gw-2026-03-15-01

Mike K.: summary of root cause (preliminary): predictor regression allowed speculative prefetch to request >1M tokens; continuous-batcher didn't cap inflight tokens; combined with prefetch allowed kvcache to fill and escalate to OOM. Triage points: (a) predictor change needs revert or fix, (b) add strong invariants in batcher to prevent >100k inflight tokens per tenant, (c) run scale tests for long prompt patterns.

Sara L.: customer impact: three hosted tenants saw degraded responses and 502s for long-run generation jobs for ~18 minutes peak. No Dedicated/private customers affected. CS notified and drafting message for affected tenants (Mike/Sara to own).

Xavier R.: oncall notes: hotfix steps performed: prefetch disabled, eviction aggressive, batcher config set (max_batch_tokens=4096, inflight=12), per-tenant cap enforced. health checks green on canary after 2 mins. promoting to prod.

Mike K.: metrics now: kvcache.total_keys trending down, avg mem.rss per node reduced 45%, generation error rate back to baseline 0.3%. Leaving a watch for 2 hours.

Jordan P.: taking handoff for ongoing monitoring. next steps for morning shift: revert predictor commit or patch predictor to respect the new upper bound, add unit/integration tests for predictor->prefetch behavior, add alert on per-tenant seq length > 200k, and follow up with postmortem.

Mike K.: thanks all. escalation checklist completed. I'll open the postmortem and link the runbook. also creating customer incident notes in Zendesk.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident transitioned to watch mode. oncall owner now: Jordan P. Severity lowered to P2 at 21:10 UTC. Links: runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/kvcache-oom ; ci-ticket: RB-7891 ; cs-ticket: CS-3392

Jordan P.: taking over — will run a controlled replay of the failing workload on staging and coordinate a predictor revert if tests reproduce. ping me for any regressions. :thumbsup:

Mike K.: handing off. signing off from urgent action. :wave:

ops-bot: note: nodes that OOMed were recycled and replaced. please validate any lost telemetry for the 20:40-20:50 window.

Sara L.: adding follow-ups to the POV: 1) temporary mitigation to remain for 2h, 2) revert predictor by EOD if no regression, 3) postmortem draft by tomorrow. I'll attach logs and heap dumps to RB-7891.

Jordan P.: acknowledged. closing active page. continuing watch. :eyes:
